open_points.subject: Trial corpus growth and function activation
open_points.text: “activation ... requires an `admitted` verdict over the current corpus”; “the corpus only grows”; “The current activation of a contract version is the one recorded last”
open_points.question: When a trial case is added after an implementation was admitted and activated, what happens to that activation now that its verdict no longer covers the current corpus?
options: Keep the activation runnable until another implementation is submitted
Immediately rerun admission and keep or replace the activation from the result
Leave the activation record but make the contract version unrunnable until an implementation is admitted over the enlarged corpus
open_points.default_guess: Leave the activation record as history but make the contract version unrunnable until admission over the enlarged corpus.

open_points.subject: Try implementation
open_points.text: “try an implementation | agent | trial evidence per case”; “admit and activate | kernel, when an implementation is submitted”; “every active case of the corpus is run again for the implementation at admission time”
open_points.question: What implementation does the separate `try` action operate on, and does it create or persist an Implementation before admission?
options: Try an already persisted Implementation over the whole current corpus
Try submitted code transiently without creating an Implementation
Submission itself performs both try and admission, so there is no distinct product action
open_points.default_guess: Try an already persisted Implementation over the whole current corpus and keep the resulting TrialExecutions without changing admission or activation.

open_points.subject: M17 ProofResult
open_points.text: “Substitution: proving the same version gives the same result”; “whether a flow version whose proof failed because a binding was not yet accepted can be proven again later — closed by A05 (yes)”
open_points.question: Is a ProofResult identified only by `flow_version_id`, or must it also identify the mutable proof context under which the result was computed?
options: One replaceable/on-demand result per flow version
A distinct result for each proof evaluation
A value identified by the flow version plus the relevant binding-state snapshot
open_points.default_guess: Treat each computed result as an observation tied to the relevant binding-state snapshot.

open_points.subject: M23 NodeExecution
open_points.text: M23 says “Identity: value” and “an attempt's record is issued once”; M07 says “an execution is an observation ... Entity issued once, not a value”
open_points.question: Is NodeExecution a value interchangeable by equal facts, or an entity representing one issued observation?
options: Value identified by its full facts
Entity identified by `(run_id, node_id, map_index, attempt_number)`
open_points.default_guess: Entity identified by `(run_id, node_id, map_index, attempt_number)`.

open_points.subject: M07 TrialExecution file outputs
open_points.text: “for a `file` port only its facts — digest, size and media type”; “Every value carries `open`, `business_confidential` or `personal_data`”; “a trial case's expected output [takes] the highest class among that case's inputs, as a trial execution's output does”
open_points.question: Does each file output recorded by a TrialExecution also carry its disclosure class?
options: Include the disclosure class in each recorded file-output fact
Derive the class solely from the trial inputs and do not record it
Trial file outputs are exempt from carrying a disclosure class
open_points.default_guess: Include the derived disclosure class in each recorded file-output fact.

open_points.subject: M24 EffectApproval preview
open_points.text: “`preview`: what the owner saw — operation, target service, the built request and the input values”; “Persistence candidate: Durable”; “The only files the kernel keeps beyond a run are the file fixtures of trial cases”
open_points.question: When an approved operation has a file input or another payload whose bytes are removed with the run spool, what durable facts does the approval preview retain?
options: Retain only references, digests, classes and bounded metadata
Retain the complete request and input bytes permanently
Retain the complete preview only until the run spool is emptied, then keep metadata
open_points.default_guess: Retain only references, digests, classes and bounded metadata; obtain previewable file bytes from the live spool.

open_points.subject: M24 request digest and credentials
open_points.text: “the fully built request as the owner was shown it — method, URL, headers and body”; “The credential's value is never shown, so rotating it voids nothing”; “`request_digest`: the digest of the fully built request shown”
open_points.question: Are credential-bearing headers excluded from the request facts and digest covered by an approval, and if so which representation of those headers is included?
options: Exclude credential values entirely while including only stable header names or placeholders
Include credential values in the digest but not the displayed preview
Exclude all credential-bearing headers from both preview and digest
open_points.default_guess: Include stable header names or placeholders but exclude credential values from both preview and digest.

open_points.subject: K-11 MCP surface
open_points.text: “one fixed set of typed operations over `mcp`: inspect, author, try, run, resume, read traces, and the owner's approve, accept, activate, grant, revoke, resolve and cancel” while the primary actions also name “capture a failed execution”, “release a failed run”, “roll a slot back”, “propose an operation binding”, and “compose and prove a flow”
open_points.question: Which MCP product operation exposes each primary action omitted from K-11's asserted fixed set?
options: Each omitted action is a separate fixed MCP operation
Some or all omitted actions are modes of `author`, `inspect`, or `activate`
The omitted primary actions are not exposed over MCP
open_points.default_guess: Treat authoring, binding proposal, flow composition, capture, release and rollback as explicitly named fixed MCP operations.

open_points.subject: Implementation inspection and repair context
open_points.text: “inspect functions ... | owner, agent | typed description”; “For repair an agent receives one contract, its current implementation and that slot's recent traces and trial evidence”; “code ... shown to the agent repairing its slot”
open_points.question: May an owner or agent inspect arbitrary implementation source, or is source readable only for the current implementation of a slot selected for repair?
options: Owner and agents may inspect every stored implementation body
The owner may inspect every body, while an agent receives only the current body in a repair context
Both owner and agent receive implementation bodies only through the one-slot repair view
open_points.default_guess: The owner may inspect every body; an agent receives only the selected slot's current implementation in the repair view.

open_points.subject: K-12 recent repair evidence
open_points.text: “its current implementation and that slot's recent traces and trial evidence”
open_points.question: Which traces and trial evidence count as `recent` and are therefore returned to the repairing agent?
options: All retained evidence for the slot
A fixed most-recent count
Evidence within a fixed time window
Evidence selected explicitly by the requesting agent
open_points.default_guess: Return all retained evidence for the selected slot unless a later query explicitly requests a subset.
